title: Selective Protection and Labelling of Arginine/Lysine Side Chains in HBSs of Proteins
author: Phuong Thao Bui
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wq6fdze
materials: PGO (Merck Ltd., UK, 97%) was used in the dark, as it is light sensitive. PGO was freshly prepared in 50% (v/v) DMSO, 50% (v/v) HPLC grade water at 1 M, which was then diluted to 0.5 M and then 0.2 M with 0.2 M NaHCO 3, pH 9.5. The pH was adjusted by 0.1 M NaOH to between 9.1 and 9.5 to ensure optimal reaction. The heparin mini column was rinsed with 30 μL of the 0.2 M PGO solution to exchange buffers. A further 30 µL PGO solution was added to the column and the bound protein was allowed to react for 60 min at room temperature in the dark. The reaction was quenched with 5 μL 0.1% (v/v) Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) in water so that the final concentration of TFA is 0.01% (v/v). The mini-column was then washed with 200 μL Na-1 buffer (4 x 50 μL). Bound proteins were eluted with 2 x 20 μL Na-2 buffer (2 M NaCl, 0.2M NaHCO 3, pH 9.5) containing 0.1% (w/v) RapiGest SF Surfactant (Waters, UK). The addition of surfactant was important to ensure protein recovery in this and subsequent steps, due to the increased hydrophobicity of the protein following PGO conjugation to arginine side chains. 0.2 , PGO 60:00:00, React in the dark Phenylglyoxal hydrate Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #142433-5G RapiGest SF Surfactant Contributed by users

For labeling, protein was buffer exchanged by four cycles of dilution on 3.5 kDa-MWCO centrifugal filters with 400 μL 10-fold diluted 0.2 M NaHCO 3, pH 9.5 containing 0.1% (w/v) RapiGest and 3 cycles of dilution with 400 μL HPLC water containing 0.1% (w/v) RapiGest by centrifugation at 13200 rpm for 10 min. After freezing at -80°C for 30 min, the sample was lyophilized for an hour. (merckmillipore, UFC500396, 3.5 kDa-MWCO centrifugal filters)

Peptides were concentrated by rotary evaporation to a final volume of 10 μL and desalted using C18 Zip-Tips(Millipore). C18 Zip Tips were first pre-wetted with 2 x 10 μL 100 % (v/v) acetonitrile and then pre-equilibrated with 2 x 10 μL 0.1% (w/v) TFA in water. The peptides were loaded on the Zip Tip, the loading was repeated 7 to 8 times to ensure binding. The Zip Tip was washed with 10 μL 0.1% (w/v) TFA. Finally, the peptides were eluted with 2 μL of 5mg/mL α-cyano-4-hydroxycinnamic acid (CHCA, > 99% purity, Sigma) in 50:50 acetonitrile/water + 1%TFA, straight onto a 96 spot MALDI (matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionisation) target plate. Analyses were performed on the instrument Synapt G2-Si (Waters, Manchester, UK) with MALDI source equipped with a frequency tripled Nd:YAG UV laser (λ = 355 nm), operating at 1 kHz. The spectrum acquisition time was 120 seconds, with 1 second scan rates, laser energy of 150 Au. The MS spectra were extracted by MASSLYNX v.4.1 (Waters, Manchester, UK) with the spectrum range from 500 Da to 4000 Da. The spectra were then processed using automatic peak detection including background subtraction.

steps.title: Prepare mini affinity column
steps.instruction: Create a mini affinity column using AF-heparin beads (binding capacity 4 mg antithrombin III/mL).

substeps.instruction: Place a plastic air filter as a frit at the end of a P10 pipette tip
Pack the tip with 20 μL AF-heparin beads, ensuring no bubbles are present inside the column

steps.title: Equilibrate column
steps.instruction: Equilibrate the mini-column using Na-1 buffer (200 mM NaCl, 0.2M NaHCO3, pH 9.5).

substeps.instruction: Dispense 4 × 50 μL of Na-1 buffer slowly into the column using a 2 mL sterile syringe

steps.title: Load FGF protein
steps.instruction: Load a minimum of 10 μg FGF protein onto the column (estimated loading capacity 15 mg/mL).

substeps.instruction: Repeat the loading process 3 times to ensure binding between protein and heparin beads

steps.title: Wash column
steps.instruction: Remove unbound protein by washing the column with 200 μL (4 x 50 μL) of Na-1 buffer.

steps.title: Concentrate eluted protein
steps.instruction: Prepare the eluted protein for reaction by adjusting volume and concentration.

substeps.instruction: Dilute eluted protein with 400 μL 0.2M NaHCO3, pH 9.5
Concentrate the solution to a final volume of 90~100 μL using a 3.5 kDa MWCO centrifugal filter

steps.title: Perform HPG reaction
steps.instruction: React the protein with HPG in a dark room, maintaining pH over 9.0.

substeps.instruction: Incubate 80 μL of diluted protein with 20 μL 0.5M HPG (final HPG concentration 0.1 M)
Incubate for 60 min at room temperature in the dark
Quench the reaction with 5 μL 0.1% (v/v) TFA in water

steps.title: Dissolve and denature protein
steps.instruction: Prepare the freeze-dried protein for digestion.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve protein in a mixture of 80 μL 25 mM NH4HCO3 and 10 μL 1% (w/v) RapiGest (~0.1% w/v final)
Centrifuge quickly at 3200 rpm for 30 seconds

steps.title: Reduce and alkylate proteins
steps.instruction: Perform reduction and carbamidomethylation of the proteins.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 μL 50 mM DTT (5mM final concentration) and incubate for 15 min at 56°C
Add 5 μL 0.1M freshly made iodoacetamide and incubate for 30 min in the dark

steps.title: Digest proteins
steps.instruction: Perform protein digestion using chymotrypsin at a ratio of 1:100 overnight.
